questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error,select 'No Error'.**

Several visitors are (1)/ expected to visit the (2)/ trade fair this weekend. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **No Error**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The subject "**Several visitors**" is correctly used in the plural form, which aligns with the verb "**are**."
 
• The phrase "**expected to visit**" is grammatically correct and appropriately placed.
 
• The object "**the trade fair**" is properly used and contextually makes sense.
 
• The phrase "**this weekend**" correctly specifies the time frame for the event.
 
• The overall sentence structure is clear and coherent, adhering to the rules of grammar.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select No Error.**

Our professor taught us that (1)/ one should respect the (2)/ religion of others as much as his own. (3)/No error (4)/
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the pronoun ‘his’ is incorrect and must be replaced with ‘one’s’ as the sentence previously states ‘one should.’ It should read as:’..religion of others as much as one’s own.’ Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

No sooner had she arrive that her (1)/ friends arranged a reception in her (2)/ honour in the best resort in the town. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the structure of ‘no sooner’ has been violated. It should be ‘no sooner did she arrive’ or ‘no sooner had she arrived.’ Here the verb ‘arrive’ in simple present tense is incorrect and must be replaced with the verb in simple past tense ‘arrived.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

During India's struggle for (1)/ freedom many brilliant students (2)/ gave up their studies by Bhagat Singh's call. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the preposition ‘by’ is incorrect and must be replaced with ‘on’ to convey the correct meaning.

By=> in a particular way or means of

On=> as something takes place

It should read as ‘gave up their studies on Bhagat Singh’s call.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Tell me (1)/ what all you know about it (2)/ before I take a decision in the matter. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the preposition ‘in’ does not fit here and must be replaced with ‘regarding.’ ‘In’ has a different usage and ‘regarding’ means ‘related to.’ Thus it should read as:’before I take a decision regarding the matter’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with a blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Suman has _____ for the final round of the competition.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Superior=> of the highest quality

Decided=> to choose something, especially after thinking carefully about several possibilities

Declared=> openly or formally asserted or announced.

Qualified=> officially recognized as being trained to perform a particular job; certified.

Thus 4 fits here conveying the correct meaning that someone got officially recognized to go to the final round of the competition.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Her supporters began to _____ and she was left alone.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the phrasal verbs are:

Fall over=> fall to the ground

Fall away=> reduced

Fall off=> a decrease in something.

Fall on=> depend

Thus option 2 fits here meaning that the supporters began to decrease.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

No _____ than fifteen boys failed in a class of forty.
questions.solution: The noun ‘boys’ here is countable so ‘few’ or ‘fewer’ are applicable here. Options 1 and 2 are used for uncountable nouns. The word ‘fewer’ is correct here as the structure of ‘no..than’ always has the adjective in comparative form.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Sania was compensated _____ the loss of her belongings at the airport.
questions.solution: The correct preposition here is ‘for’ as someone or something is compensated ‘for’ something. ‘Compensated for’ means ‘give (someone) something, typically money, in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury incurred; recompense.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Suraj is acquainted _____ Kapil.
questions.solution: The correct preposition here is ‘with’ as someone is ‘acquainted’ with someone. It means ‘knowing or being familiar with a person.’ The other prepositions are incorrect here. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Gumption
questions.solution:
The word ‘gumption’ means ‘shrewd or spirited initiative and resourcefulness.’ The other words mean as follows:

Acumen=> skill or shrewness

Starry=>full of or lit by stars.

Futile=> of no use; yielding no result

Fallow=> uncultivated

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Laconic
questions.solution:
The word ‘laconic’ means ‘brief.’ The other words mean as follows:

Shrewd=> having or based on a clear understanding and good judgment of a situation, resulting in an advantage

Whim=> a sudden desire or change of mind, especially one that is unusual or unexplained.

Climax=> the most intense, exciting, or important point of something; the culmination

Concise=> brief

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Valedictory
questions.solution:
The word ‘valedictory’ means ‘last or final’. The other words mean as follows:

Hesitant=> reluctant

Terminal=> end or extreme

Ridicule=> mock or make fun of

Deception=> treachery

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Amateur
questions.solution:
The word ‘amateur’ means ‘non-professional’ or ‘novice’. The other words mean as follows:

Beginner=> novice

Weary=> tired

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Denouement

The word ‘denouement’ means ‘finale or ending’. The other words mean as follows:

Systematic=> arranged or methodical

Improper=> unsuitable

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Bucolic
questions.solution:
The word ‘bucolic’ means ‘relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.' The other words mean as follows:

Rustic=> relating to the ountryside; rural.

Dull=> boring

Tranquil=> peaceful

Fierce=> ferocious

Thus option 4 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given**

Compendium
questions.solution:
The word ‘compendium’ means ‘collection or compilation’. The other words mean as follows:

Expansion=> enhancement

Reference=> the action of mentioning or alluding to something

Precis=> a summary or abstract of a text or speech.

Outline=> border

Thus option 1 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Chastise
questions.solution:
The word ‘chastise’ means ‘to criticize or rebuke.’ The other words mean as follows:

Praise=> laud or worship

Resist=> withstand the action or effect of

Prefer=> like (one thing or person) better than another or others; tend to choose

Repel=> loathe

Thus option 1 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

The word ‘daunt’ means ‘demoralize or discourage’. The other words mean as follows:

Rejoice=> celebrate

Encourage=> support

Decrease=> reduce

Discard=> reject

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Oblivious
questions.solution:
The word ‘oblivious’ means ‘unaware.’ The meanings of the other words are:

Hideous=> extremely ugly

Victorious=> having won a victory; triumphant.

Conscious=> aware

Advantageous=> beneficial

Thus option 3 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

An iron will
questions.solution: The idiom ‘an iron will’ means ‘a fixed decision or a firm opinion.’ He had the ‘iron will’ to get to the top of the hill.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Get into a soup
questions.solution: The idiom ‘get into a soup’ means ‘to get into trouble.’ Thus 1 is the correct answer. He got into a soup when the teacher caught him using the cell phone in class.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Haul over the coals
questions.solution: The idiom ‘haul over the coals’ means ‘to scold.’ Taylor was hauled over the coals for wasting police time.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

To carry the day
questions.solution: The idiom ‘to carry the day’ means ‘to succeed.’ After spending weeks constructing my project, I was thrilled to carry the day at the science fair.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Go over
questions.solution: The idiom ‘go over’ means ‘review.’ He went over my science project and explained certain parts to me.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Neha was too clever to (see through Rohan's tricks).
questions.solution: The phrase ‘see through’ means ‘understand something implied or indirect.’ The sentence has been structured correctly. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

He has been working (off and on) for several years on this theory.
questions.solution:
The correct phrase is ‘off and on’ which means ‘intermittently; sometimes.’

The other options are incorrect. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

(Having had) in the USA Embassy for a long time, Mr. Gupta has met many prominent

personalities.
questions.solution: The correct option here is option 2 which means Mr.Gupta was in the USA Embassy for a long time. The pronoun ‘he’ cannot fit in this structure of the sentence thus option 1 is eliminated. Option 3 gives the sense of a condition which is not met by the given sentence. Thus it is incorrect as well.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

I am definitely late, the bus (will have left) the bus stop by the time I reach there.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4).**

__
 
• We use **will have** when we are looking back from** a point in time in the future**:

 
 
• ***By the end of the decade, scientists will have discovered a cure for influenza.***__
 
• __***I will phone at six o'clock. He will have got home by then.***__
 
 
 
• or looking back from the present:
 __
 
• ***Look at the time. The match will have started.***__
 
• __***It's half-past five. Dad will have finished work by now.***__
 
 

__***​​***__In the given sentence, we are looking back from the present so, **"will have"** should be used here.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The guest stood quietly for (few) moments.
questions.solution: ‘Few’ means ‘almost nothing or none’ which does not make any sense here. ‘A few’ means ‘small or a small amount’. It means that the guest stood quietly for some moments. Option 3 is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

Dictatorship=> absolute rule

questions.question:

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Select the incorrectly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The **correct answer** is **option 3 **i.e. '**Emanicipation**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **incorrect spelling **is '**Emanicipation**'.
 
• The **correct spelling **is '**Emancipation**'.
 
• **Emancipation**: (मुक्ति) the act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.
 
 
• **Example**: "The emancipation of women was a major social change."
 
 

Therefore, the **correct answer **is - **Emanicipation**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Embarrassment**- a feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.
 
• **Exasperation**- a feeling of intense irritation or annoyance
 
• **Fermentation**- the chemical breakdown of a substance by bacteria, yeasts, or other microorganisms, typically involving effervescence and the giving off of heat.

questions.question: feelings pure and with _____ unworldly.
questions.solution:
The word here must be a noun as can be understood from the sentence. Thus the adverbs ‘passively’ and ‘religiously’ are eliminated. Thus either 1 or 4 will fit here.The meanings of the words are:

Ambitions=> aims

Passively=> in an accepting manner, without active response or resistance

Religiously=> in a way that relates to or conforms with a religion.

Resources=> a stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

The sentence talks about feelings and humane objects thus ‘ambitions’ fits in the context. ‘Resources’ is incorrect here.

questions.question: then able to _____ the world with feelings pure
questions.solution: The word ‘challenge’ is a misfit here as nothing challenging is mentioned in the context. The word ‘roam’ means ‘wander’ and makes no sense here. The word ‘target’ means ‘aim’ and does not fit here. The word ‘face’ means ‘tackle or deal with’ and conveys a proper meaning that we can face the world with pure feelings.

questions.question: It is the great formative _____ of our life, brief but powerful.
questions.solution: The word ‘lesson’ means ‘a teaching’ and youth is not a lesson. The word ‘resource’ means ‘a stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively’ and makes no sense here. The word ‘period’ which means ‘a length or portion of time’ and fits here correctly. The word ‘idea’ means ‘a thought or suggestion as to a possible course of action’ and does not convey any meaning here. Thus option 3 is the correct answer

questions.question: Let us _____ in it.
questions.solution: The word here should be such that it goes with the preposition ‘in’. Thus ‘rejoice’ which means ‘to celebrate’ fits here. The other words make no sense if used with ‘in.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Youth is the _____ gift of the god,
questions.solution: The word here must have a positive meaning as can be understood from the sentence. Thus ‘best’ fits here and ‘useless’ would be wrong here. The word ‘inexpensive’ means ‘cheap’ and does not fit here. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which country's name is not mentioned in the passage?

questions.question: When was the Antarctic Treaty signed?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘*The Antarctic Treaty was signed in 1959 and creates the rules for the exploration of the Antarctic.’ *Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Why was Antarctic Treaty signed?

options.text: to ban dumping of nuclear waste
to create rules for its exploration

questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage that the treaty was signed to protect the continent, to prevent all sorts of harmful human activities and to set up rules for exploration. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Why did environmentalists have fear of exploiting Antarctica for military and economic reasons?
questions.solution:
It is mentioned in the passage '

*Environmentalists fear that exploiting Antarctica for military and economic reasons **will damage the environment***.' Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, the reserves of which mineral is not found under the Antarctic ice?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘In addition, economic experts claim that there are large amounts of coal, nickel and copper under the Antarctic ice.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer as ‘iron’ is not mentioned.
